contract: Bridgey Protocol v1, native newline JSON transport, as spoken by Bridgey by Round Robin
contractStatus: draft for v0.10 (stabilisation), to be frozen at 1.0; last reviewed 2026-10-27

statuses.upstream-v1: Shipped by upstream Bridgey 0.5/0.6. Meaning, fields and limits change only through a new feature key, because upstream peers depend on them; frozen at 1.0.
statuses.edition-extension: An optional field the edition adds to an upstream-v1 message. Upstream peers ignore it.
statuses.edition-draft: Edition only, gated by a *_draft1 feature key. Sent only to peers that advertise the key. May change until accepted upstream, then moves to a final key.
statuses.retired: No longer sent or advertised. Receivers keep ignoring it; the key and its kinds are never reused.
statuses.designed: Specified in docs/protocol.md but not implemented by either client yet. Never sent.

directions.sender-to-receiver: From the side that sends a folder (the Mac today) to the side that receives it (the phone today).
directions.receiver-to-sender: From the folder receiver (the phone today) to the folder sender (the Mac today).
directions.controller-to-host: From the remote control controller (the phone) to the host (the Mac).
directions.host-to-controller: From the remote control host (the Mac) to the controller (the phone).

transport.framing: UTF-8 JSON object per line, terminated by LF; a CR before LF is ignored
transport.onMalformedFrame: close the session before dispatch (oversized frame, invalid UTF-8, not a JSON object, missing or wrong-typed envelope field)
transport.onUnknownKind: ignore the message and keep the session
transport.onUndecryptablePayload: upstream-v1 messages, folders/places and browsing close the session; clipboard offers, codes and remote input drop the message and keep the session
transport.replayWindow: per session, the last 256 accepted messageId values, oldest evicted first

sessionId.note: empty only in pairing.cancel sent before the session ID is known

messageId.note: UUID; required by every encrypted message that uses the replay window. An empty optional string counts as absent

sequence.note: an integral JSON number; each kind checks its own range

commitment.note: protocol 2: base64 SHA-256 commitment to the first-pairing offer's ephemeral key, opened by pairing.reveal

protocolVersion.note: in pairing.offer and pairing.answer: the highest protocol the sender speaks; absent means 1

tag.note: protocol 2: base64 HMAC-SHA-256 over the sender's device ID and every other envelope field, on every frame after pairing when both ends sent protocolVersion 2

features.note: the device serves browsing (places.files, media.*, places.download) and accepts uploads; Macs advertise it false
the device accepts folders.offer from its peer; phones check it before sending a folder to a Mac

the Mac sets it when Mac actions is on and granted to that phone (off by default), the phone when its Mac actions switch is on for that Mac; gates actions.*. Both apps keep it as a switch, but a non-boolean value reads false like every draft key
the Mac understands quick.request links action open (Open on Mac); set while Web links is on for that phone. Phones advertise nothing
the device understands focus.state; advertised while either Focus direction (share, follow) is on
the phone takes photos for that Mac (its switch, on by default); the Mac sets it while Files is on for that phone; gates camera.*. The photo comes back over files.v1 with cameraRequestId

messages.notes: Sent by the side that dials. targetDeviceId (edition extension) names the trusted peer a reconnect is for; any other receiver closes quietly. Protocol 2: a first pairing sends commitment instead of publicKey, and reveals the key in pairing.reveal after the answer.
Protocol 2 first pairing: the initiator's ephemeral key after the answer. The responder checks it against the offer's commitment and fails the pairing on a mismatch.
proof is an HMAC under the pairing key; signature is P-256 over the session transcript.
Ends only the session it arrives on.
messageId echoes the ping's. Connection health (both apps) times the round trip from it; health puts nothing new on the wire and has no feature key.

payload.features: object of feature key to boolean; see features

messages.notes: Sent after pairing and whenever local policy changes. A feature is available only when both peers report true.

payload.(raw): UTF-8 text, not JSON, 1 to 32,768 bytes

messages.notes: text plus html at most 32 KiB.
messageId is the acknowledged message's ID.
Clipboard is off locally; followed by features.update.

payload.items: array of 1 to 100 {index, kind: text|html|image|file, mime (1 to 255 chars), name? (files, 1 to 255 chars), size (0 to 10 GiB), sha256? (base64 of 32 bytes), inline? (base64, all inline items at most 16 KiB decoded)}

payload.transferId: string, UUID chosen by the receiver

payload.code: expired | changed | too_large | unavailable | disabled | busy

payload.name: string, display name, last path component only
payload.purpose: edition extension: "clipboard" with offerId and index
payload.cameraRequestId: edition extension (camera_draft1): string, UUID of the Mac's open camera.request that this photo answers; older Macs ignore it and simply receive a file

messages.notes: Files is off locally; sent without decrypting the offer, followed by features.update.

payload.(raw): file bytes, at most 24 KiB per chunk, sequence from 0 without gaps

messages.notes: Cumulative. The Mac keeps at most 64 chunks unacknowledged.

payload.sha256: string, base64 SHA-256 of all bytes

messages.notes: Idempotent.

payload.title: string, at most 1,024
payload.applicationIcon: string, optional base64 PNG, at most 28 KiB encoded
payload.actions: array of at most 4 {actionToken (at most 64), title (at most 64), allowsReply}
payload.redacted: boolean, edition extension, only with smsDefaultApp true

messages.notes: Content is sensitive and never logged.
Android runs only tokens it retained for the still active notification.

payload.reason: when not ok: bluetooth_off | unauthorized | unsupported | failed

payload.action: string (links: offer, or open to a Mac that advertises links_open_draft1; media: toggle | pause | next | previous | seek | volume)
payload.value: string (links: http(s) URL, at most 4,096 bytes; seek 0 to 604800; volume 0 to 100)
payload.sequence: integer, 1 to 2^53-1, per feature high-water mark

messages.notes: Edition extension (links_open_draft1): Open on Mac sends links action open. The Mac opens the link at once only when its own Open links from phones right away setting is on (off by default), at most one link per phone every 3 seconds; otherwise it queues the link like offer.

payload.opened: edition extension (links_open_draft1): boolean, true when the Mac opened the link right away; older phones ignore it

payload.title: string, at most 256 chars
payload.artwork: string, optional base64 JPEG, at most 16 KiB, at most 128x128

messages.notes: messageId is the request's ID. Senders time out after five seconds.

payload.number: string, 3 to 15 digits with optional leading +; spaces, parentheses, dots and hyphens are removed

messages.notes: At most one request every three seconds.
A phone that receives it answers input.session.stop, reason unsupported.

payload.reason: user | left_screen | screen_off | local_stop | timeout | disabled | permission_required | busy | invalid | unsupported

payload.text: string, 1 to 256 scalars, at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, no Cc characters; never logged

payload.key: left | right | up | down | return | escape | tab | space | backspace | page_up | page_down | home | end | f5 | previous_app

payload.action: next | previous | start | end | black | laser_on | laser_move | laser_off
payload.x: integer 0 to 10,000 with laser_on and laser_move
payload.y: integer 0 to 10,000 with laser_on and laser_move

payload.actions: array of at most 64 {id, title, blocked?}. id: lock | sleep | screensaver | volume_up | volume_down | volume_mute | volume_set | app:<bundle id, [A-Za-z0-9.-], 1 to 155> | shortcut:<lowercase UUID>. title: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters, required for app: and shortcut: (phones show their own titles for the fixed ids). blocked: only permission_required (Lock without Accessibility)
payload.volume: optional {level: integer 0 to 100, muted: boolean}, while volume is allowed and the output has a settable volume

messages.notes: What this phone may run now; it replaces the previous list. Sent after each features.update that shows the key on both sides, and whenever the list, a switch, the grant or a permission changes. The phone drops single entries with an unknown id, a missing or bad title or a repeated id, and the whole catalog for a wrong version or more than 64 entries.

payload.action: string, an id from the latest catalog
payload.sequence: integer, 1 to 2^53-1, per session high-water mark, checked after the messageId window

messages.notes: Only an identifier from the Mac's own list goes on the wire: no command, argument, Shortcut name or text. A run that fails the version, requestId or sequence check is dropped; anything else gets exactly one actions.result. Rate limits per phone: volume 10 at once then 5 a second, other actions 3 at once then one every 2 seconds. The phone waits 10 seconds for the result (70 for a Shortcut), then reports it not confirmed.

payload.reason: with refused: not_allowed | invalid | rate_limited | busy | permission_required | unavailable | failed; phones read anything else as failed
payload.volume: optional {level, muted}: the volume after a volume action

messages.notes: The Mac keeps a private audit log of every run and refusal (owner-only, 30 days, at most 500 entries, never the value).

payload.active: boolean: the phone's Do Not Disturb (any interruption filter but all), or the Mac's Focus

messages.notes: Sent only while the sender's share switch is on and the peer's latest map shows the key: once after each features.update that shows it on both sides, then on every change. Applied only while the receiver's follow switch is on; a follower does not report the change it just made for 10 seconds, so two followers cannot loop.
One open request per Mac, at most one every 3 seconds; it expires after 2 minutes. The phone opens the camera only when unlocked and after a tap. A malformed request is dropped without an answer.

payload.status: opened | locked | permission_required | cancelled | busy | disabled | sending | failed; the Mac drops an unknown status

messages.notes: The photo itself arrives as a files.offer carrying cameraRequestId.

payload.purpose: optional "browse" (files_browse_draft1): every place whatever the destination mode, plus writable, media and documents in the answer

payload.places: array of at most 17 {placeId, label (64), available, freeBytes}
payload.defaultFreeBytes: integer or null, free bytes where a send would land by default (every answer)
payload.writable: boolean, purpose browse only: "Allow other devices to change files here"
payload.media: purpose browse only: full | partial | none (photo and video access)
payload.documents: boolean, purpose browse only: at least one place is indexed for recent documents

payload.folders: array of folder names, at most 500 per page

payload.code: error code, see docs/protocol.md (browse adds read_only)

messages.notes: Also the failure answer to every browse request (places.files, media.*, places.download). Browse requests from a Mac whose files_browse_draft1 the phone did not advertise answer unsupported; over a lane budget, busy.

payload.placeId: string, default or a granted place
payload.cursor: string or null, opaque, from the previous page

messages.notes: Browse lane: 4 in flight and 40 per 10 s, else busy; answered within 8 s. Served in every folder destination mode. Errors not_found, place_unavailable, policy.

payload.entries: array of at most 200 {name (one existing component, 1 to 255 bytes), dir (boolean), size (integer, null for folders), modified (Unix ms or null), mimeType (null for folders), thumb (boolean)}

messages.notes: Folders first, then files, each in sort order (names case-insensitive, then exact). Hidden items and part files are neither listed nor counted.

payload.items: array of 1 to 100 refs ({placeId, path, name} or {mediaId}); a folder brings its subtree, hidden and system files skipped and counted

messages.notes: Browse lane. The phone then sends folders.offer with into: true and downloadRequestId; the Mac accepts a download offer only when it asked for it. Errors not_found, place_unavailable, limit_exceeded, busy, policy.

payload.folderTransferId: string, UUID of the folders.offer that follows

payload.kind: media (photos and videos, newest first) | files (recent documents in indexed places) | recent (both)

messages.notes: Browse lane.

payload.items: array of {ref, name, size, modified (Unix ms), mimeType, width, height, durationMs (null when unknown), thumb (boolean), location (display path, at most 128 characters)}
payload.access: full | partial | none (photo and video access; none returns no media items)
payload.indexing: boolean, the document index is refreshing

messages.notes: Askers cache by device ID, ref, modified and size: the same four always mean the same bytes.

payload.items: array of 1 to 64 {key (1 to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-], chosen by the asker), ref}
payload.replaces: string, optional, requestId of an earlier media request it cancels

messages.notes: Media lane: 4 active and 60 per 10 s, else busy. Answers are low priority: sent only while no file chunk, acknowledgement or control message waits.

payload.thumbs: array of {key, mimeType (image/webp from Android 11, else image/jpeg), width, height, tint (#rrggbb average colour), data (base64, at most 24 KiB decoded)}
payload.missing: array of keys without a thumbnail
payload.done: boolean, true on the last batch

messages.notes: In the order asked; as many thumbnails as fit in each batch. 45,056 bytes of plaintext keep the frame under the 65,536-byte limit after AES-GCM and base64.
Media lane. Videos answer with the poster frame. Errors not_found, unsupported.

payload.data: string, base64, at most 32 KiB decoded per part

messages.notes: Consecutive parts; the whole preview is at most 1 MiB.

payload.ref: ref to a file, not a folder

messages.notes: Media lane. Ranges are previews (hover prefetch, streamed playback) and carry no hash; a saved copy always goes through places.download.

payload.modified: integer, Unix ms, the whole file
payload.data: string, base64, at most 32 KiB decoded
payload.last: boolean, end of the range or of the file

payload.requestId: string, the media request to cancel

messages.notes: Not answered. Parts already on the wire may still arrive and are dropped by the asker.

payload.into: boolean, optional, default false (files_browse_draft1): entries land directly in the destination, top-level clashes saved as copies, nothing merged, replaced or asked
payload.downloadRequestId: string, UUID, optional (files_browse_draft1): the offer answers that places.download of the receiver

messages.notes: The Mac checks folders_draft1 before sending to a phone, the phone folders_receive_draft1 before sending to a Mac (no destination: a Mac serves no places). Uploads are into with destination; a phone rejects them read_only while it does not allow changes, policy while browsing is off.

payload.entries: array of at most 256 {type: dir | file, path, size?, sha256?, modified?}

payload.choices: array of merge | replace | new_folder | cancel

payload.completedBitmap: string, base64, bit i set when entry i is done
payload.freeBytes: integer or null, free bytes at the chosen destination (files_browse_draft1)

messages.notes: With Files off the receiver sends it outer only, without decrypting the offer.

payload.records: object of key to {value, changedAt, version, changedBy}
